question.text: In the Battles of Issus and Gaugamela, Alexander defeated Darius III, the ruler of this large empire centered on modern-day Iran.
question.answerHtml: the First Persian Empire [or the Achaemenid Empire, or Xšāça]
question.clue: King Psamtik III was defeated at the battle of Pelesium near the Nile Delta by a ruler of this empire named Cambyses II.

swap.leadin: A military operation in this country called Operation Eagle Claw was authorized only when Secretary of State Cyrus Vance took a brief vacation and was not present to oppose the plan.
swap.text: Name this country that took 52 Americans hostage in 1979 and released them moments after Ronald Reagan was sworn in as President in 1981.
swap.clue: Notable tourist attractions here include the cities of Isfahan, Qom, Shiraz and Tabriz.

question.leadin: Just decades after the Message of Muhammad, the Caliphate defeated two of the greatest empires in the world.
question.text: Name this Persian Empire that was decisively beaten at the Battle of the Chains, al-Qadisiyah, and Nahavand. This dynasty succeeded the Parthians, although the exact circumstances are still unclear.
question.clue: This empire was defeated at Qadisiyyah at the hands of Umar's general, Khalid ibn al-Walid.

swap.leadin: Give the following related to first Persian invasion of Greece.
swap.text: This "Great" Persian leader, who avenged the death of Cyrus the Great by attacking Scythia, invaded Greece after the Ionian Revolt.
swap.clue: He reorganized his empire into twenty satrapies and successfully defeated revolts in Babylon and Ionia after his ascension to the throne.

question.leadin: This ruler's namesake cylinder, which describes how Marduk chose him to defeat the Babylonian king Nabonidus, is sometimes considered the first charter of human rights.
question.text: Name this Persian ruler who founded the Achaemenid empire after defeating Astyages, the last king of the Medes, in a revolt. In the Bible, the Book of Ezra claims that he freed the Jewish captives in Babylonia.
question.clue: Another kingdom conquered by this ruler fell while being led by Croesus, king of the Lydian empire.

swap.text: One Persian king with this name expanded the empire to its greatest extent and organized it into 20 satrapies. Another king with this name was the last king of the empire after losing the battles of Issus and Gaugamela.
swap.clue: One figure of this name faced off against generals like Parmenio and had one of his underlings, Bessus, attempt a coup against him.

question.leadin: Troops of this empire poured molten gold down the throat of a captured commander.
question.text: Name this empire that won the Battle of Carrhae while commanded by Surena and Silaces.
question.clue: A train of camels bearing arrows helped this state win a major victory, after which its forces poured molten gold down an invading general's throat.

swap.leadin: Apocryphally, the blood of followers of this religion was used to power mills and create bread during the conquest of Gorgan.
swap.text: Name this religion whose followers began converting to Islam after the fall of the Sassanids and Arab conquest of Persia.
swap.clue: The Sassanids proselytized this state religion of theirs, though it did not spread as far as Manichaeism or Christianity. This religion venerates Ahura Mazda.

question.leadin: The third and fourth kings of this name were separated from their rule by Pharnaces I.
question.text: Give this name for six kings of Pontus, the last of whom massacred 80,000 Romans in Anatolia and prompted Sulla, Murena, and Lucullus to fight three namesake wars against him.
question.answerHtml: Mithridates [or Mithridates the Great; or Eupator Dionysius from any confused folks]
question.clue: After conquering the territory of Nicomedes IV of Bithynia, a king of this name massacred all of its Roman citizens in the "Asiatic Vespers".

swap.text: One of Alexander's successors was this general, who founded a namesake empire which ruled the Levant, Anatolia, and Mesopotamia under kings like Antiochus Epiphanes.
swap.clue: He dispatched the ambassador Megasthenes on expeditions to the east, resulting in the production of theIndika.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the generals who carved up Alexander the Great's empire after his death, the Diadochi.
question.text: This man managed to grab the lion's share of the empire, taking Mesopotamia, Persia, and Bactria. He later fought an unsuccessful war with Chandragupta Maurya.
question.clue: This ruler, one of Alexander the Great's successors, who established a namesake Hellenistic kingdom in western Asia and was succeeded by his son Antiochus I.

swap.leadin: One member of this dynasty made Philip the Arab surrender to him.
swap.text: Name this dynasty which fought the White Huns, and sponsored Zurvan Zoroastrianism. Under Khosrau I, many reforms were enacted, while under Khosrau II, the dynasty reached it territorial zenith, eventually falling after the Battle of Qadisyyah.
swap.clue: Its last great ruler was deposed by Bahram, but with the help of Emperor Maurice regained the throne.

question.leadin: Heleen Sancisi-Weerdenburg argued that historians relied exclusively on Greek sources on this empire and that there was no solid evidence of its actual existence.
question.text: Name these people who, according to Herodotus, built the capital of Ecbatana and were last ruled by Astyages before his Persian grandson overthrew him around 550 BC.
question.clue: Early kings of these people included Deioces and Phraortes.

swap.text: The Behistun inscription is written in Old Persian, Babylonian, and the language of these peoples, whose capital was Susa. This civilization's Old dynasties included the Awan, Simashki, and Epartid.
swap.clue: The "Lament for Ur" describes a conquest by these people, whose Shutrukid dynasty later defeated the Kassites and looted the stele bearing the Code of Hammurabi from Babylon.

question.leadin: On the Letoon ("LET-oh-on") stele, the inscription in this language explicitly calls Pixodarus satrap of Caria and Lycia, rather than just Lycia in the Greek and Lycian versions.
question.text: Name this major administrative language in the Achaemenid bureaucracy. This Northwest Semitic language was also used in letters by Arshama, satrap of Egypt.
question.clue: Demons found in the Ginza Rabba were repelled using ceramic bowls with incantations in this language.

swap.text: Darius' rise to power is described in the Bisitun inscription, which claims that Gaumata, one of these people, pretended to be Smerdis, the brother of Cambyses II. These people, who in Sasanian times were led by a chief figure called the mowbed, are described by Herodotus as one of six Median tribes.
swap.clue: Important to both the Medes and Persians were this priestly class which accomplished feats of prophecy, dream-interpretation, and sorcery later named for them.

question.leadin: Name these things about the Parthian Empire.
question.text: A man of this name fought a war against Izates and perhaps codified the Avesta as part of an Iranian Revival. The sixth and last Parthian king of this name faced trouble from the Sassanid Adrashir I.
question.clue: Septimus Severus defeated the fifth Parthian emperor with this name. The sixth emperor of this name would be defeated by the Sassanids in the early third century CE.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Alexander the Great's career after Gaugamela.
swap.text: In this city in western Iran, Alexander arranged a mass, and massively unpopular, wedding between his Macedonian soldiers and Persian women. Cyrus the Great captured this former capital of the Elamite Empire.
swap.clue: A polity that called itself Haltamti transferred its capital from Anshan to this city, and this "great holy city" suffered a brutal sack by Ashurbanipal.

question.text: Valerian lost at Edessa to the first Sassanid ruler of this name, the son of founder Ardeshir I, who prompted Gordian's murder by Philip the Arab after winning the Battle of Misiche but saw his harem raided by Balista. The second ruler of this name fought Pap and Arshak II of Armenia and killed Julian the Apostate outside Ctesiphon.
question.clue: A king with this name built a namesake city on the road between Estakhr and Ctesiphon.

swap.leadin: Name these titles of nobility or rulership, FTPE.
swap.text: This was the term in Achaemenid Persia for a provincial governor and is still an expression for anyone who has control of a large enclave.
swap.clue: 26 positions with this title were established around 580 BCE, a number that later increased to 36 according to the Behistun Inscription.
